title: Road Markings & Studs
whatItIs: Lines along the road show where you may cross, overtake and stop. Coloured studs help at night, especially on wet roads.

keyFacts.text: Chevrons bordered by a solid white line: you MUST NOT enter except in an emergency.
Yellow box: you MUST NOT enter until your exit road or lane is clear.

keyFacts: No stopping on roads with double white lines, even if your side is broken, except to drop off, pick up or load.
A double red line ALWAYS means no stopping at any time.
Studs: white = lanes or centre, red = left edge, amber = central reservation, green = lay-bys and slip roads.

visual.caption: Double white lines: read the line nearest you

items.label: Centre line
items.meaning: Cross only to overtake or turn off, if clear.

items.label: Hazard warning line
items.meaning: Longer lines, shorter gaps: hazard ahead.

items.label: Broken line near you
items.meaning: May cross to overtake if safe.

items.label: Solid line near you
items.meaning: MUST NOT cross or straddle (exceptions: Q1).

a.label: Hatching, broken border
points: Don't enter unless necessary and safe
Separates lanes or protects traffic turning right

b.label: Chevrons, solid border
points: MUST NOT enter except in an emergency
Used where slip roads leave and join motorways

onTheTest.question: The line nearest you in a set of double white lines is solid. When may you cross it, if the road is clear?
options: To overtake a cyclist doing 10 mph or less
To overtake a tractor doing 20 mph
To overtake any vehicle if you can see ahead
To get a better view ahead
onTheTest.why: Rule 129: if the road is clear you may cross to pass a stationary vehicle, or a pedal cycle, horse or road maintenance vehicle at 10 mph or less.

onTheTest.question: You want to turn right at a yellow box junction. When may you enter the box and wait?
options: When your exit is clear and only oncoming traffic stops you
Only when the box is empty
onTheTest.why: Rule 174: you may wait in the box to turn right when only oncoming traffic, or others waiting to turn right, stop you. KYTS: only if your exit is clear.

traps: The 10 mph exception covers only pedal cycles, horses and road maintenance vehicles, not slow cars.
At a signalled roundabout you MUST NOT enter the box unless you can cross it completely without stopping.
Red and single yellow lines are only a guide: check the signs. No days shown? It applies every day.
